subject: Operational evidence and subprocessor gating for model-improvement opt-out
messages:
From: Laurie Chen <laurie@medivate.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.inference>
Date: Mon, 12 Jan 2026 10:02:00 -0800
Subject: Evidence for DPA change: model-improvement opt-out and subprocessor gating

Hi Evelyn,

Thanks again for the quick call last week. Procurement and security asked that I follow up with a concrete list of the operational evidence they need before we can sign the DPA amendment that includes the explicit model-improvement opt-out and prompt/response custody language. High-level ask list below — can your team provide these artifacts or a timeline?

1) Current subprocessor inventory (name, function, region, last attestation date). CSV preferred.
2) Ops checklist showing how the "no-training"/opt-out is enforced (KV/ephemeral routing, batching controls, and sample request traces showing KV cache bypass).
3) KMS residency plan and proof that customer keys can be routed onshore (onboarding checklist or attestation).
4) SFTP export plan + a test account for a one-time export to validate export pipeline (we prefer US-only destination).
5) Annotated DPA redline indicating where Redwood commits not to use prompt/response pairs for model updates and how derivative rights are scoped.

We can accept a combination of documents and short recordings (5–10 minutes). Procurement would like this by EOD Thursday 1/15 to keep the timeline. Let me know if that timeline is impossible and which items you can provide sooner.

Attachments: medivate_security_q1.xlsx (we'll send our questionnaire if helpful).

Best,
Laurie
Director, Security & Procurement
Medivate Health

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.inference>

Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.inference>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.inference>

Subject: Re: Evidence for DPA change: model-improvement opt-out and subprocessor gating

Hi Laurie — thanks for the clear list. We can put together the requested artifacts; we already have a standard ops-proof pack for no-training commitments that maps to items 1–3.

Quick clarifying questions before we gather everything:
- For KMS residency, do you need a customer-managed key (bring-your-own-key) workflow, or is an attestation that keys remain in a US KMS sufficient for procurement?
- For the SFTP export test, confirm whether Medivate will accept time-limited credentials to a staging bucket for validation versus doing an on-prem push.

I'll loop in Kimberly and David to prepare the DPA redline and the ops checklist. Can we schedule a 30-minute call Tue 1/13 11am PT to walk through the artifacts? If that works, I'll send a calendar invite.

Regards,
Evelyn Hart
Head of Customer Solutions
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Evidence for DPA change: model-improvement opt-out and subprocessor gating

Hi Laurie / Evelyn — attaching the materials I mentioned on the call. Short summary below and next steps.

Attachments included: 
- dpa-redline-annotated.docx (track changes showing our proposed opt-out wording and the prompt/response custody carveout)
- redwood_subprocessor_list_20260110.csv (current inventory, function column included)
- ops-proof-checklist.pdf (operational artifacts we can provide: routing logs, KV bypass traces, BaaS config snippets, and a sampling of request IDs with sensitive fields redacted)

Summary:
- We will accept an attestation that Medivate requires US-only residency for the data flow; based on that we will provide an onshore routing plan and a KMS residency attestation. If you need customer-managed keys (BYOK) we can scope that as an addendum — it will take additional onboarding (estimate 3–4 weeks).
- For the model-improvement opt-out, the redline includes our operational fallback (use of locked model variants + logging-only telemetry) and a description of how prompt/response pairs are excluded from model training pipelines.

Requests from our side:
- Please return the completed medivate_security_q1.xlsx so our security team can map gaps.
- Confirm whether the SFTP validation must be to an on-prem destination or if a US cloud staging bucket is acceptable; we will provision temporary credentials for either.

We can also provide a short recording (6 min) that walks through the ops-proof-checklist if that helps procurement/security. Happy to run through the redline on the call.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security
Redwood Inference

(Attachment stubs: dpa-redline-annotated.docx, redwood_subprocessor_list_20260110.csv, ops-proof-checklist.pdf)

From: Laurie Chen <laurie@medivate.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.inference>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.inference>
Cc: procurement@medivate.com
Date: Tue, 13 Jan 2026 13:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Evidence for DPA change: model-improvement opt-out and subprocessor gating

Kimberly — thanks for the quick turnaround and the attachments. I've shared the redline with legal; procurement had a couple of follow-ups before we take the call: 

1) Derivative rights: legal wants a plain-language confirmation that Medivate retains ownership of outputs and that Redwood will not assert additional model rights over customer prompts/responses. Your redline looks promising but they asked for a short clause we can include in the SOW if helpful.
2) Residency: we can accept a US cloud staging bucket for the SFTP validation; procurement will do the actual export verification.
3) Evidence format: would prefer URL links to a shared drive folder with logs + the ops checklist rather than large PDFs.

I've attached our medivate_security_q1.xlsx filled out for your team — we've only marked a few items as risky and added comments in column H where we need clarification. Also: any chance you can add a webhook or a monitoring flag that notifies Medivate if an internal process marks a request as eligible for model-improvement later on? That would make our internal compliance checks easier.

Attachments: medivate_security_q1.xlsx

Best,
Laurie
